turns.t: Good morning. I'd like to review my situation. I have stress-related stomach upset and headaches, and I want to know whether my medication is the right one.
Good morning. Tell me which medication you're currently taking for this.
Propranolol, 40 mg, twice a day. It was started by my previous doctor.
How long have you been taking it?
About four months.
What do you think it has done for you? ~
The headaches are less frequent. The stomach is much the same. ~
Understood. What is going on in your life at the moment? ~
I've taken on a new role at the firm, with a lot more responsibility. I'm working until nine most nights. ~
That is a lot. And how are you eating and sleeping? ~
I skip lunch. Dinner is late. I sleep about five hours. ~
Do you have any other health conditions I should record?
Asthma, since childhood. It's been quiet for years.
That is important, because propranolol can make asthma worse. Have you noticed any wheeze or chest tightness since starting it? ~
No, none. ~
Good. I'd still like to review the choice of medicine with you. ~
What are my options? ~
There are other medicines for preventing headaches that don't affect the lungs, and for the stomach, the first step is regular meals and managing stress. ~
I'd rather avoid anything that makes my asthma worse. ~
I agree. I'd suggest we stop the propranolol gradually and switch to something else, but I'd like to check some bloods first.
Which bloods? ~
A full blood count and a check on your liver, thyroid and kidneys, to make sure there's nothing else behind the symptoms.
That's reasonable. ~
Please do not stop the propranolol suddenly, because that can cause problems.
Understood. ~
I'd also like you to have a proper lunch each day, and try to leave work on time at least twice a week.
I'll try, though I make no promises. ~
I'd like to see you again in two weeks, when the results are in, and we'll decide on the new medicine together.
Two weeks. Thank you. ~
In the meantime, if you notice any wheeze or breathlessness, come in at once.
Will do. ~
